Subject: Deal sprint: GPU burst balance & short-window commit coordination

Hi all,

Quick one as Acme's pilot is moving faster than the baseline forecast and they asked for an optional two-week surge in June. High level: Acme is willing to sign a short-term, smaller commit for a higher-burst allowance — they need ~120 GPU-days over a 14-day window (peak days ~12-14 GPUs).

Asks:
- Ben: can you sketch what burst headroom looks like in the week of Jun 8–21 given current reserve bookings?
- Karthik/Infra: what are the operational constraints for enabling a short-window burst on Dedicated (time to provision, limits on fractional allocations, fallback to hosted)?
- Laura/Finance: does a two-week premium burst with a nominal short commit (30-day invoice) fit into our current AR/discount guardrails?

I've attached Acme's short-window usage forecast. Rebecca — adding you to keep expectations clear on timings.

Thanks,
Tessa
--
Tessa Morgan
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com

On Tue, May 18, 2026 at 09:02 AM tessa_morgan@redwood.com wrote:
> Quick one as Acme's pilot is moving faster...

Short summary from me after looking at pools: we have two nearby reserve pools that could be rebalanced for a 2-week window with limited customer impact if we accept a temporary 15% degradation buffer on peak throughput for non-critical customers. Numbers:
- Baseline free burst headroom (week of Jun 8): ~8 GPUs avg available across regions; worst-case contiguous availability for 14 days: ~6 GPUs.
- If we relocate low-priority trial capacity and apply sprint-mode compression on long-tail jobs, we can free ~10 additional GPUs for up to 10 days, or ~7 GPUs for 14 days.

Implication: to meet Acme's peak days (~12–14 GPUs) we need either:
A) formal short-term burst credit (prepaid) + limited reserve rebalancing (preferred), or
B) downgrade some pre-production customers temporarily (operationally painful).

I attached a quick spreadsheet with scenarios. I also flagged two deals (DealId: PINE-210, HAZ-77) that would be impacted by rebalancing — worth a quick check.

Ben
attachment: scenario_summaries.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: rebecca.li@acme.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-20T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal sprint: GPU burst balance & short-window commit coordination

Thanks — quick infra note:
- Provisioning delta: for Dedicated we can schedule an isolated pool change (reallocation + network config) in ~48–72 hours if we pre-approve the nodes and IO paths. For <14-day bursts, it's operationally simpler to use hot-standby hosts in our burst pool (already configured) and assign capacity via routing policy.
- Limits: the routing layer caps per-customer contiguous GPUs at 20 for fairness; we are fine for Acme.
- Risk: KV cache warmup could add 100–200ms p50 latency on first 10–20 requests during peak start; recommend a soft-warmup window (pre-batch 500 prompts) if predictable start time.

Operational asks:
1) Ben: confirm which low-priority pools are acceptable to compress (we need names).
2) Laura: if finance signs off on a prepaid mini-commit, we can treat this as a timed reconfiguration and activate burst nodes using the hot-standby route.

Karthik
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: rebecca.li@acme.com, finance-pm@acme.com
Date: 2026-05-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal sprint: GPU burst balance & short-window commit coordination

Receipt and initial finance view:
- Short-term prepaid commit (14 days) is acceptable; recommend an "accelerated-burst" SKU: flat prep-paid fee + usage overage billed at premium rate. This avoids long-term discounting and preserves AR guardrails.
- Pricing suggestion: $35/GPU-hour for the burst window (vs our baseline reserved $18/GPU-hour) with a minimum 80 GPU-hours prepayment (~equivalent to partial coverage of the 120 GPU-days requested).
- Approvals: I can green-light up to $35k in one-off credits without exec sign-off; anything above requires Finance Director approval.

Action: Tessa, if Acme signs the short commit doc (I can draft one-pager), we can provision on Karthik's timeline. Please confirm if Acme accepts premium pricing.

Laura

Rebecca — thanks for the quick replies during the sprint. Short summary and next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Summary:
- Infra can enable the burst using hot-standby nodes within 48–72 hours (Karthik) assuming prepayment confirmation.
- Ben's scenario analysis shows we can reach Acme's peak by combining reserve rebalancing + prepaid burst credits; small impact to two low-priority deals (ben flagged).
- Finance proposes an accelerated-burst SKU ($35/GPU-hour). Laura can approve up to $35k in credits.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Acme to confirm acceptance of accelerated-burst SKU and sign one-page short-commit (Rebecca, please review by Tue, May 25).
2) Tessa to circulate one-pager + DocuSign link (I'll draft and loop Laura).
3) Ben to finalize pool names to compress and publish the exact rebalancing list (by Thu, May 23).
4) Karthik to schedule hot-standby activation window contingent on signed prepay (target activations: Jun 8 start).

Rebecca — are you ok for me to send the one-pager and DocuSign? If yes, I'll include the proposed invoice and activation dates so infra can start staging.

Cheers,
Tessa
